scheme_name: Education Loan Scheme under NSFDC- Haryana
description:
The Education Loan Scheme under the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC) in Haryana was launched to provide financial assistance to students from Scheduled Castes (SC) and other backward classes (OBC) who wish to pursue higher education.

The scheme was initiated in the year 2007 to empower students from marginalized communities by facilitating access to quality education.

The primary objective of the Education Loan Scheme is to promote higher education among SC and OBC students by providing them with financial support for tuition fees and other educational expenses.

The scheme aims to cover the entire cost of education for eligible students, including tuition fees, books, and other necessary expenses.

The maximum loan amount available under this scheme is up to INR 10 lakh for students pursuing professional courses.

For students enrolled in non-professional courses, the maximum loan amount is capped at INR 5 lakh.

The interest rate on loans under this scheme is set at a subsidized rate of 4 percent per annum.

The repayment period for the education loan is flexible, allowing students to repay the loan over a period of up to 10 years after completion of their education.

Eligibility criteria for the Education Loan Scheme include being a resident of Haryana and belonging to the Scheduled Caste or Other Backward Class category.

Applicants must be between the ages of 18 and 35 years at the time of applying for the loan.

The family income limit for eligibility is set at INR 3 lakh per annum for Scheduled Castes and INR 6 lakh per annum for Other Backward Classes.

Students must have secured admission to recognized institutions for higher education, either in India or abroad, to qualify for the loan.

The application process for the Education Loan Scheme involves several steps.

First, applicants must obtain the application form from the official NSFDC website or the nearest NSFDC office.

The completed application form must be submitted along with required documents, including proof of identity, proof of income, and admission confirmation from the educational institution.

Additional documents may include caste certificates, bank account details, and any other documents specified by the NSFDC.

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the concerned authorities at the NSFDC.

The loan approval process typically takes around 15 to 30 days from the date of submission of the application.

Disbursement of the loan amount is done in installments based on the academic calendar of the educational institution.

Funds are usually released directly to the institution to cover tuition fees and other educational expenses.

The scheme also includes provisions for a moratorium period during which no repayment is required.

This moratorium period lasts for the duration of the course plus an additional six months after completion of the course.

The implementing authority for the Education Loan Scheme is the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation.

The NSFDC operates under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India.

For any queries or assistance, applicants can contact the NSFDC office at their headquarters in New Delhi.

The contact number for NSFDC is 011-2338-1016 and the official website is www.nsfdc.nic.in.

The Education Loan Scheme has been instrumental in increasing the enrollment rates of SC and OBC students in higher education institutions across Haryana.

According to reports, the scheme has benefited over 10,000 students since its inception.

The government has allocated a budget of INR 50 crore for the fiscal year 2023-2024 to support this scheme.

The scheme is part of the larger initiative by the Government of India to promote education among marginalized communities and reduce the dropout rates in higher education.

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme also aims to provide guidance and counseling to students regarding career options.

The NSFDC collaborates with various educational institutions to facilitate workshops and seminars for students.

The Education Loan Scheme is aligned with the National Policy on Education, which emphasizes the need for equitable access to education.

The scheme also aims to reduce the financial burden on families from marginalized communities, enabling them to invest in their children's education.

The loan amount can be utilized for various educational expenses, including tuition fees, hostel fees, and purchase of books and equipment.

Students are encouraged to maintain a good academic record to ensure continued support under the scheme.

The NSFDC also provides a platform for students to share their experiences and success stories, promoting the benefits of education.

The Education Loan Scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries, with many expressing gratitude for the financial support provided.

The government continuously reviews and updates the scheme to ensure it meets the evolving needs of students.

In recent years, there has been an increase in the number of applications received under the scheme, indicating a growing awareness among students.

The Education Loan Scheme is a crucial step towards achieving the goal of inclusive education in India.

The scheme not only supports individual students but also contributes to the overall development of society by empowering marginalized communities through education.

The NSFDC has established a network of regional offices across Haryana to facilitate the application process and provide assistance to students.

These regional offices are equipped with trained staff to guide applicants through the process and answer any queries.

The Education Loan Scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to promoting education as a fundamental right for all citizens.

Overall, the Education Loan Scheme under NSFDC in Haryana plays a vital role in bridging the educational gap for SC and OBC students, ensuring they have the opportunity to pursue their academic aspirations without financial constraints.
